rubric: ItemRow declares @Binding var item: Item and owns no @State copy of it
The parent produces a per-element binding (List($items) or $items[index]) rather than passing a copy
The Toggle is bound to $item.done, so flipping it mutates the parent array
items stays @State in the parent and is not duplicated in the child
notes:
One question, asked precisely: do you know the difference between a value and a *write path* to a value?

Traps:

- **`@State private var item: Item` in the row.** It compiles, the toggle animates, and nothing is saved — the row is flipping its own copy. This is the single most common SwiftUI bug in review.
- **`ForEach(items) { item in ... }`.** `item` there is a copy; there is no binding to hand down. You need `List($items)`, `ForEach($items)`, or an index-based `$items[index]`.
- **Indexing by position when the array can be reordered or filtered.** `$items[index]` is safe here, but the `Identifiable`-driven `$`-binding is what survives a sort.
- If asked to go further: `Binding(get:set:)` written by hand is the honest explanation of what `$item.done` desugars to — a getter and a setter, not a stored value.
